20.7.4.3 Reactions of Esters

Following are some of the important reactions of esters.

(i) Hydrolysis

Esters are commonly hydrolyzed to carboxylic acid and alcohol, on heating with water very slowly. However the hydrolysis of ester can be catalyzed by an acid or base.

The acid-catalyzed hydrolysis is reversible, and is the reverse of acid-catalyzed esterification (Section 18.1.7.4 and 20.7.1.3).

The alkaline hydrolysis will yield a salt of carboxylic acid and alcohol. This reaction is also called saponification reaction, because such type of reaction is used for preparation of soap from fats.

(ii) Reduction of Esters

Ester can be reduced to alcohols in the presence of strong reducing agent such as lithium aluminum hydride in ether (Section 18.1.5.6).

(iii) Reaction of Ester with Grignard Reagent

Esters react with two equivalents of Grignard reagent to give an alcohol (Section 17.2.3.2).

20.7.4.4 Reactions of Amides

Amides are the least reactive of the common carboxylic acid derivatives. Like other acid derivatives, amides can also reacts with nucleophiles like water.

(i) Hydrolysis

Amides on hydrolysis form the corresponding carboxylic acids and ammonia. The reaction is very slow and requires the use of strong acid or base as catalyst. Both are irreversible and in case of base catalyst, salt of carboxylic acid is obtained.

(ii) Reduction

Amides can be reduced to primary amines in presence of lithium aluminium hydride (Section 17.3.5.2.3).

20.7.4.5 Reactions of Nitriles

Alkyl nitriles or simply nitriles are also considered as derivatives of carboxylic acids. The following are some of the important reactions of nitriles.

(i) Hydrolysis

Hydrolysis of nitriles with aqueous acid or base yields a carboxylic acid. In the presence of base catalyst, the final product is actually salt of carboxylic acid (Section 20.5.2).

(ii) Reduction

Nitriles yield primary amines when reduced with catalytic method, or using lithium aluminium hydride in ether (Section 17.3.5.2.1).

(iii) Reaction with Grignard Reagent

Nitriles on reaction with Grignard reagent produce ketones. The strongly nucleophilic Grignard reagent add to carbon-nitrogen triple bond in a similar fashion to that seen in aldehydes and ketones. The reaction proceeds via an imine salt intermediate, which is further hydrolysed to give ketones.

20.7.4.3 Reactions of Esters

Following are some of the important reactions of esters.

(i) Hydrolysis

Esters are commonly hydrolyzed to carboxylic acid and alcohol, on heating with water very slowly. However the hydrolysis of ester can be catalyzed by an acid or base.

The acid-catalyzed hydrolysis is reversible, and is the reverse of acid-catalyzed esterification (Section 18.1.7.4 and 20.7.1.3).

The alkaline hydrolysis will yield a salt of carboxylic acid and alcohol. This reaction is also called saponification reaction, because such type of reaction is used for preparation of soap from fats.

(ii) Reduction of Esters

Ester can be reduced to alcohols in the presence of strong reducing agent such as lithium aluminum hydride in ether (Section 18.1.5.6).

(iii) Reaction of Ester with Grignard Reagent

Esters react with two equivalents of Grignard reagent to give an alcohol (Section 17.2.3.2).

20.7.4.4 Reactions of Amides

Amides are the least reactive of the common carboxylic acid derivatives. Like other acid derivatives, amides can also reacts with nucleophiles like water.

(i) Hydrolysis

Amides on hydrolysis form the corresponding carboxylic acids and ammonia. The reaction is very slow and requires the use of strong acid or base as catalyst. Both are irreversible and in case of base catalyst, salt of carboxylic acid is obtained.

(ii) Reduction

Amides can be reduced to primary amines in presence of lithium aluminium hydride (Section 17.3.5.2.3).

20.7.4.5 Reactions of Nitriles

Alkyl nitriles or simply nitriles are also considered as derivatives of carboxylic acids. The following are some of the important reactions of nitriles.

(i) Hydrolysis

Hydrolysis of nitriles with aqueous acid or base yields a carboxylic acid. In the presence of base catalyst, the final product is actually salt of carboxylic acid (Section 20.5.2).

(ii) Reduction

Nitriles yield primary amines when reduced with catalytic method, or using lithium aluminium hydride in ether (Section 17.3.5.2.1).

(iii) Reaction with Grignard Reagent

Nitriles on reaction with Grignard reagent produce ketones. The strongly nucleophilic Grignard reagent add to carbon-nitrogen triple bond in a similar fashion to that seen in aldehydes and ketones. The reaction proceeds via an imine salt intermediate, which is further hydrolysed to give ketones.
